# Stock & Flow
Visual stock-and-flow editor and systems dynamics simulator.
Guide: https://stockandflow.live/guide
Library: https://stockandflow.org/
API schema: https://stockandflow.live/api/schema
Health: https://stockandflow.live/api/health

Use GET /api/models/catalog for the searchable metadata index and GET /api/models/{id} for definitions. POST /api/validate inspects inputs without saving. POST /api/simulate runs an explicit model or model_id. POST /api/analyze/statistics computes statistics. CRUD and XMILE import/export remain available under /api/models. AI generation and modification require an existing configured provider.

MCP Streamable HTTP: https://stockandflow.live/mcp/
Legacy SSE: https://stockandflow.live/mcp/sse
Transport information: https://stockandflow.live/mcp/info
Local stdio: python -m app.mcp_server
Tools: list_models, get_model, validate_model, investigate_model, simulate_model, compare_scenarios, analyze_model, export_model_xmile, generate_model_from_description, modify_existing_model.
Resources: systems://guide, systems://engine, systems://workspace-guide and systems://models/{id}.
Prompt: investigate_system.
Numerical tools do not write models or call AI providers. AI tools return unsaved drafts.

Agent-driven pages (HTTP/SSE): open_workspace returns a private page_url and workspace_key. Open the URL, inspect_workspace, make targeted edits with edit_workspace_elements and expected_revision, run_workspace, then set_workspace_view. Check browser.applied_revision and browser.view to verify what appeared. update_workspace_model replaces a whole private draft when explicitly intended. close_workspace revokes the private session. Page tools use the user's own agent and no server-side AI account. They never write to the saved library. Session keys are private capabilities; idle expiry is one hour and a server restart ends sessions. Local stdio supports numerical tools but interactive pages require the HTTP/SSE connection.

Always inspect initial values, equations, flow endpoints, units and sources. A completed numerical run does not establish scientific validity. Library defaults include unresolved references, unsupported functions and unstable scenarios. Public status badges are bound to exact model-file hashes.

Euler and RK4 honor configured start, end and dt. Smoothing and fixed-duration material delays support Euler/RK4. Fixed history delays and random functions require Euler. Set time_settings.random_seed (integer 0..4294967295) for reproducible stochastic runs; results return the effective random_seed. POST /api/investigate and investigate_model compare full horizons at dt, dt/2 and dt/4, without modifying inputs; stochastic path convergence is excluded. Reports include model/engine hashes, missing definitions, domain and topological conservation leads. Bounds: 500 explicit elements, 100,000 intervals, 100,001 retained samples, one million retained scalar values and one million work units including hidden stages and random calls (RK4 charges five evaluations per interval). Invalid inputs and unresolved equations produce explicit errors. XMILE import supports a scalar subset and rejects unsupported behavior such as arrays, queues, conveyors and explicit nonnegative constraints.

Version 1.9 contracts: variable.role="report" evaluates a report-only numeric value or label at retained states. Results include report_values separately from numeric variables; MCP samples both channels at the same indices. Single quotes delimit labels. Reports cannot feed any equation; stateful/random calls are rejected in reports. Reports have explicit work and text budgets. Numeric dynamics remain finite and strict.

time_settings.discrete_period declares an exact recurrence period. Require Euler, dt equal to that period, and a whole number of intervals; API overrides and targeted workspace edits preserve the contract. Investigation reports fractional refinement as inapplicable. Save as JSON: XMILE rejects report outputs and fixed-period contracts explicitly.

Radau is an explicit bounded stiff solver with relative/absolute error tolerances; its output interval is not its internal integration step. Compare tolerances as well as outputs. Unsupported random/history, time-driven forcing, state-driven lookup forcing and uncertified state jumps in the RHS are rejected. Failure reports preserve causal errors, exact settings and engine fingerprints. Partial settings inherit omitted saved values. XMILE translates supported functions and syntax, rejecting lossy conversions. The full public 1.9 audit completes 1,050 of 1,078 definitions, with 28 explicit failures; source fidelity and empirical calibration must still be assessed separately.
